scope: Individual RGB colors, layer inheritance, camera sectors, cable flags, symbol library, persistence, undo/redo and DWG/DXF colors. Existing camera and design workflows rechecked. Full viewer/unit-detection suite was previously accepted in 1.3.0 and was not repeated for this focused change.

checks: Existing v1 overlay opens unchanged with inherited camera, point and text colors
Camera color changes only the selected instance and its actual sector pixels
Color selection is one undoable and redoable edit
Reset restores layer inheritance while other cameras retain their individual overrides
Cable and linked flags support a custom color or the layer color
Points and text have independent colors, including arbitrary RGB values
Locked layers disable color changes and resetting
Saving a colored camera in the library preserves its color on the next placement
A library camera can also inherit the destination layer color
Colors, inheritance and reusable library definitions persist on disk and after restart
Create a named drawing overlay layer
Middle-button panning during cable drawing stops on release and preserves the draft
Cable clicks create one route and a live total-length flag
Dragging a route vertex updates its length from 10 m to 8 m
Undo and redo restore the full route
Add an extra route-linked length flag
Move a length flag independently from its cable geometry
Draw a custom camera symbol, save its model and FOV, and place an instance
Edit camera rotation, range and size with a visible field of view
Move a camera together with its field of view
Add an installation point and editable text
Duplicate, delete and undo a drawn object
Save a reusable cable type in the local library
Overlay layers can be hidden and locked without editing the base drawing
Overlay geometry and metadata are persisted on disk
Another drawing has independent working layers
Restart restores the drawing overlays and reusable library without manual merging
Closing with an unfinished route completes and persists it before quitting
Placing a camera immediately selects it and exposes move/aim controls
Clicking the camera name selects an existing camera
Drag the camera center to move it without changing direction
Rotate the on-canvas direction handle while preserving position, FOV and range
A complete rotation gesture is one undoable and redoable change
Shift snaps direct rotation to 15-degree increments
Rotation controls remain usable after zooming
Move button previews then places the camera with a single click
Point at a world location to aim the camera without creating another instance
Escape and right-click discard aim and movement previews
Cancelling a drag also prevents its temporary position from reaching autosave
Locked camera layers reject direct manipulation
Camera position, direction and settings survive application restart
DXF keeps exact RGB colors on cameras, sectors, cables and flags
DXF export contains the base, editable cable vertices, length flags, camera and Polish labels
Exported DXF reopens as ordinary CAD geometry without its local overlay
DWG retains exact RGB colors after conversion and independent WASM parsing
A real AutoCAD 2018 DWG reopens through the independent LibreDWG WASM reader
Overlay-only export keeps the original drawing coordinates and excludes the base geometry
Cancelling the native save dialog leaves the project open and unchanged
Choosing the source file as the export destination is rejected without modifying it
No renderer errors during the complete export workflow
